The evidence explicitly states that the method's constraints prevent Gaussians from moving freely in 3D space, resulting in the failure to reconstruct areas occluded in all input images. It further clarifies that this is an 'advantage' because it allows these regions to be identified for inpainting, rather than being filled with blurry artifacts. Therefore, the claim that the method is not suitable for scenes requiring fully automatic reconstruction of all occluded regions without inpainting is directly supported by the text.
